[scale / performance / tenancy] This is a single-laptop appliance wearing a SaaS costume: one Python http.server behind a Tailscale tunnel, no payment processor, no connection pool, no rate limiting, app-level-only tenant isolation, and a single global advisory lock that serializes every audited action across all tenants on earth — it dies at ~50 concurrent users and cannot bill a dollar.

[trust for skeptics — spend controls, approvals, audit visibility, explainability, blast-radius containment] "We have beautifully-engineered locks on the doors — but the two that matter most, the money circuit-breaker and the human-approval gate, are wired to nothing and never actually fire in production."

[scale / performance / tenancy] Build/job execution: in-process daemon threads, not a durable queue: Move all builds/controller jobs onto the durable Postgres SKIP-LOCKED queue (or a real broker), executed by a SEPARATE, horizontally-scalable worker fleet. The web tier only enqueues; workers claim, checkpoint, and are crash-recoverable. Nothing long-running runs in the request process.
